reference.source: Standard endocrinology and clinical genetics references
clinicalPearls: A distinctive physical phenotype caused by variants in GNAS, which encodes the alpha subunit of the stimulatory G protein (Gs-alpha)
Characteristic features are short stature, a rounded face, obesity, brachydactyly (notably shortened fourth and fifth metacarpals), and subcutaneous ossifications

When AHO occurs with resistance to parathyroid hormone (and often other hormones such as TSH), it is termed pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1a, producing hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia with a raised PTH
The same AHO physical phenotype without hormone resistance is called pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism, reflecting the parent-of-origin (imprinting) effect of GNAS
Hormone resistance appears when the defective allele is inherited maternally, because Gs-alpha is expressed largely from the maternal allele in key tissues such as the renal proximal tubule
Ectopic dermal or subcutaneous ossification and characteristic hand radiographs (short metacarpals) are useful diagnostic clues
Management centres on correcting hypocalcaemia with calcium and active vitamin D and monitoring for associated hormone resistances
reference.pathophysiology: Albright hereditary osteodystrophy stems from inactivating variants in GNAS, the gene for Gs-alpha, the signalling protein that couples numerous hormone receptors to adenylate cyclase and cyclic AMP generation. GNAS is subject to tissue-specific genomic imprinting: in tissues such as the renal proximal tubule, expression is predominantly from the maternal allele. When the inactivating variant is maternally inherited, tissues lose most Gs-alpha activity, so hormones acting through Gs-coupled receptors (notably PTH, and often TSH and gonadotrophins) cannot signal effectively, producing multi-hormone resistance and hypocalcaemia despite elevated PTH. When the same variant is paternally inherited, imprinting preserves signalling in these tissues, so the physical AHO phenotype occurs without hormone resistance. The skeletal and soft-tissue features (brachydactyly, ectopic ossification) reflect impaired Gs-alpha-dependent signalling in developing bone and connective tissue.
additionalDifferentials: Vitamin D deficiency causing secondary hyperparathyroidism
additionalInvestigations: Serum calcium, phosphate and corrected calcium
Intact PTH level (raised in the resistance form despite hypocalcaemia)
Thyroid function tests to detect associated TSH resistance
Hand and skeletal radiographs for brachydactyly and ectopic ossification
Molecular genetic testing of GNAS with methylation studies where indicated
Family evaluation clarifying the parent of origin for counselling
redFlags: Symptomatic hypocalcaemia with tetany, seizures or prolonged QT interval
Progressive deep or disabling ectopic ossification
Untreated associated hypothyroidism from TSH resistance
reference.prognosis: With appropriate calcium and active vitamin D therapy and surveillance for additional hormone resistances, the metabolic disturbance is manageable and life expectancy is generally normal, though short stature, brachydactyly, and ectopic ossification are permanent.
pitfalls: Confusing pseudohypoparathyroidism with true hypoparathyroidism by not measuring PTH
Overlooking associated hypothyroidism because attention is fixed on calcium
Ignoring the imprinting basis, leading to inaccurate recurrence-risk counselling
Missing subtle brachydactyly or ectopic ossification that would prompt genetic testing
references: GeneReviews / OMIM entries on GNAS-related disorders
management: Correct hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia with oral calcium and active vitamin D analogues such as calcitriol or alfacalcidol in the resistance form
Thyroid hormone replacement with levothyroxine where associated TSH resistance causes hypothyroidism
Screen for and manage additional hormone resistances, including gonadotrophin and growth hormone-releasing hormone, as they emerge
Monitor serum calcium, phosphate and PTH to titrate therapy while avoiding hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis
Weight management and support for obesity, short stature and brachydactyly
Orthopaedic or dermatological input for symptomatic subcutaneous and ectopic ossifications
Genetic counselling explaining the parent-of-origin imprinting effect, with testing of relatives
